candidates.change_summary: Change the returned selector to a constant different bytes4 value so the function still completes but returns a different bytes4 than the original selector.
Return an inverted version of the original selector (bitwise NOT) so call succeeds but returns a different bytes4.
Return zero (0x00000000) instead of the expected selector so observable return differs while function doesn't revert.
Assigns baseToken only if it is currently zero (conditional), changing behavior when initialize is called on a pool already having a nonzero baseToken.
Assigns baseToken to address(0) unconditionally, overriding the provided _baseToken parameter.
Swaps assignment order: set nft first, then set baseToken after other assignments (moving baseToken assignment later), which can change baseToken if events or reentrancy observe intermediate state.
Replace assignment to nft with assignment to a different value (msg.sender) so nft becomes msg.sender instead of the provided _nft parameter.
Assign nft to address(0) instead of _nft, making nft zero after initialization.

Swap the assignments: set nft before baseToken so nft assigned from _nft but after using _baseToken unrelated—keeps nft different if ordering impacts external observation (assign nft from _baseToken instead of _nft).
Replace assignment to changeFee with assignment that doubles the input _changeFee (changeFee = _changeFee * 2), altering stored changeFee value after initialize.
Replace assignment to changeFee with assignment that sets changeFee to zero, so stored changeFee after initialize becomes 0 regardless of input.
Replace assignment to changeFee with assignment that assigns _changeFee + 1, incrementing stored changeFee by one compared to original input.
Remove the feeRate upper bound check so initialize allows any feeRate value (deleted the FeeRateTooHigh revert), which can result in a different stored feeRate after initialize.
Clamp the provided _feeRate to zero before storing, so feeRate will always be 0 after initialize regardless of input.
Invert feeRate assignment to store maximum (5000) when input is below cap, otherwise store input; this produces different stored feeRate values.

Change the check that reverts when already initialized from 'if (initialized) revert AlreadyInitialized();' to no longer revert (delete the revert), allowing re-initialization which will toggle/leave 'initialized' true but allow state to be overwritten.

Invert the already-initialized check to only allow initialization when already initialized (i.e., require initialized) so calling initialize will revert unless initialized was true, changing observable initialized value.
Move setting 'initialized = true;' to the start of the function (before checks), causing the variable to be true even if subsequent checks revert or alter behavior.
